findings_addressed.oracle: capstone.Cs(CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_64) driven directly on the same section/rva — first 5 instructions' addresses and mnemonics are compared against those returned by disasm.disassemble(count=5)
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/disassembler.py line 271: change `if len(instructions) >= count:` to `if len(instructions) >= 0:` — the loop breaks immediately, returning an empty list, causing `assert len(instructions) == 5` to fail

notes: Replaced `assert len(instructions) <= 5` (trivially true for empty list) with `assert len(instructions) == 5` (exact count gate). Added an independent capstone oracle that drives capstone.Cs directly on the same .text bytes and verifies that each of the 5 returned instructions has matching address and mnemonic. kernel32.dll .text section always has thousands of decodable x86-64 instructions, so count=5 must return exactly 5.
